::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 24 [1900]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS West Devon Area Record Office
:::

My dear [Mary](people/person_1626.qmd)
I am out in the drawing room again but no farther till the wind changes, and the cough departs, but [Helen](people/person_1613.qmd) is coming to look after me on Monday, and [Miss Finlaison](people/person_512.qmd) has done so most kindly.  By the by I never have had a headache all through so I don’t know how she came to [illegible] it-  I hope [Sydney](people/person_2178.qmd) is better -  [Augusta](people/person_1180.qmd) has begun to write letters again -  All the spring seems cut short by the weather except the catkins.

I am sorry to miss the Friday evening sermons which are on popular sayings

All is not gold that glitters
A friend in need is a friend indeed
Time and Tide wait for nobody –  I only heard the first and second and liked them much

your most affectionate
C M Yonge
